titulo: Data, LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) and choosing a vendor: where data is allowed to go
lead: Every time someone pastes a customer conversation into an AI, the data travels: to a server, sometimes outside Brazil, sometimes to train another company's model. LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) applies even when an AI is the one reading. This lesson gives you a simple way to decide where each piece of data can go and with which vendor.
objetivo: decide where a piece of data can go (closed model, open local model, or none) and fill in the data × vendor × license matrix for 1 case.

aprende.t: The 4 types of data and what each one allows
Closed via API, open local, or none: pros and cons
The LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) articles that come up most in AI projects

hero_alt: A professional chooses between three paths on the table: a locked file box, a small local server and a globe.

secoes.sub: Three questions, in order. The most restrictive answer wins.

nos.detalhe: Public (website catalog), internal (cost prices, targets), personal (identifies someone: name, CPF, phone, address) and sensitive (health, racial origin, religion, biometrics, among others). The further right it is, the fewer places it can go.

nos.sub: Closed via API, open local, free app
nos.detalhe: Closed model via API: the data goes to the vendor's server, often outside Brazil. Open model running locally: the data does not leave the company, but someone has to look after the machine. Free app with generic terms: the worst case, because the terms may allow using the data for training.

nos.sub: Terms, country, retention, use for training
nos.detalhe: For the closed one: is there a contract? In what country is the server? How long do they keep it? Do they use it for training? For the open one: does the license allow commercial use? Is there a revenue cap, or is it research only? Who published the model?

nos.sub: Goes, goes anonymized, or doesn't go
nos.detalhe: Three outcomes: it can go as is; it can go after anonymizing (swap the name for a code, remove the CPF and phone); it doesn't go. Every decision involving personal data needs a written LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) legal basis, and the company's DPO (data protection officer) should be consulted before, not after.

secoes.legenda: Anonymizing solves a lot: "Mercadinho Boa Vista, Seu Antônio, (19) 9..." becomes "Customer A, order of 10 boxes".

secoes.titulo: The LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) as it shows up in an AI project
secoes.sub: This is not legal advice: it's the minimum you need to know when to call the legal team.

passos.sub: What counts as personal and sensitive data
texto: Personal data is anything that identifies or can identify a person. Sensitive data includes health, racial origin, religious belief, political opinion, biometrics and genetics.
A customer service conversation almost always contains personal data: name, phone, address.
Every processing activity needs a legal basis: consent, contract performance, legal obligation, legitimate interest, among others. Sensitive data has narrower rules (art. 11).
Practical question: "on what basis are we sending this to the AI?" If nobody can answer, stop.

Sending personal data to a server outside Brazil is an international transfer and is only allowed in specific cases, such as contract clauses approved by the ANPD (Brazil's data protection authority).
Using an API hosted in the US or China with customer data falls under this.
Data subjects can request a review of a decision made solely by automated means that affects their interests (art. 20), such as a credit denial.
The company needs security measures to protect the data (art. 46): an exposed key and an open spreadsheet are the opposite of that.

secoes.sub: The decision matrix and the prompt for anonymizing.

blocos.conteudo:
DATA MATRIX — <case>, <date>

The case: <what you want to do with AI>
Data involved: <list> → type: <public | internal | personal | sensitive>

| Option | Where the data goes | Server country | Contract / data agreement | Used for training? | License (if open) | Cost | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Closed model via API | | | | | — | | |
| B. Open model, local | company computer | Brazil | — | no | <license> | | |
| C. Anonymize first | | | | | | | |
| D. Don't use AI | — | — | — | — | — | | |

Legal basis (LGPD art. 7 or 11): <which one and why>
International transfer? <yes/no; if yes, which art. 33 case>
Who was consulted: <DPO / legal / IT>
Decision: <option> because <reason in one sentence>

Rewrite the text below, replacing all personal data with codes:
- names of people → Customer A, Customer B...
- CPF, phone, email, address → [removed]
- customer company name → Company 1, Company 2...
Keep products, quantities, dates and the meaning of the conversation.
At the end, list what you replaced, without repeating the original data.

TEXT:
<paste here>

abas.html: Case: daily summary of Horizonte's WhatsApp conversations. Data: customers' name, phone, CPF and address → personal. Today: sent to a free service outside Brazil, with no contract, under terms that allow using the data for training. Decision: stop now; option C (anonymize first) with a vendor under contract, or B (local open model).

• "It's just a summary": the summary is made from the whole conversation, which goes along with it.
  • Free plan on customer data: the terms often allow using what you send.
  • Thinking an open model solves everything: the license may limit use, and someone has to keep the machine secure.

paragrafos: In August 2026, Alibaba released Qwen3.8-27B under the Apache 2.0 license, which allows commercial use. According to the company, with quantization it runs even on a laptop. For an SMB, this opens a fixed-cost option where the data never leaves the company.

But open does not mean risk-free. Read the license: some have a revenue cap or are research-only. Check who published the model and where it came from, and remember that the local machine needs security too.

secoes.titulo: Practice: the matrix for one case
secoes.sub: Use a case from your own company. No real case? Use the Horizonte customer service summary (F10).

exercicios.titulo: E1 · Pick the case and classify the data
exercicios.texto: Describe the case and list the data. No case? Open the Horizonte customer service summary.
exercicios.pronto: each piece of data in the case has a type: public, internal, personal or sensitive.

exercicios.texto: For option A, look in the vendor's terms for: server country, retention and use for training. For B, the license of an open model.
exercicios.pronto: the matrix has all 4 rows filled in; where you did not find the information, it says "not informed".

exercicios.titulo: E3 · Decide with a legal basis
exercicios.texto: Write the decision, the legal basis and who needs to be consulted.
exercicios.pronto: the decision fits in one sentence and names the legal basis and the person who needs to be consulted.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Juliana wants to paste conversations with customers' names and phone numbers into a free summary app. What should she do first?
opcoes: Paste them: it's only for summarizing.
Check where the data goes, the terms and the legal basis; at a minimum, anonymize it first.
Ask the customer to send fewer messages.
Use the same vendor's paid app without reading the terms.
perguntas.explica: A conversation with a name and phone number is personal data. Before sending it: destination, contract, use for training and legal basis. Anonymizing greatly reduces the risk. The common mistake is thinking that "just summarizing" is not data processing.

perguntas.p: Sending customer data to an API with a server in the US is, under the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law):
opcoes: International transfer, allowed only in the cases covered by arts. 33 to 36.
perguntas.explica: It is an international transfer and needs a permitted basis, such as contract clauses approved by the ANPD (Brazil's data protection authority). The common mistake is treating "the cloud" as if it had no country.

perguntas.p: An open model runs on the company's computer. What still needs to be checked?
opcoes: Nothing: open and local is always safe.
The license (commercial use, revenue cap), the provenance and the security of the machine.
perguntas.explica: Local solves the data's trip, not the license or the security of the machine. The common mistake is confusing "open" with "no rules".

itens.texto: What data is it? Where would it go? Under what contract and license?
Swapping a name for a code solves many cases.
The data stays put, but the license, the provenance and a secure machine still matter.
